current_evidence: The council's 'Local Validation List' download area (linked from 'Make a planning application') holds only 'Local Validation List Document - 2023', titled 'Local List of Planning Validation Requirements July 2023'. The yoursay consultation (16 Mar-14 Apr 2023) points to it as the current list, and no later draft or adoption could be found.

issues.detail: The list date is given as 2023-03-01, taken from PDF metadata. The document text dates the list July 2023. March 2023 was the consultation-draft stage (the consultation ran 16 Mar-14 Apr 2023), not the adopted list.
issues.evidence: Document title: 'Local List of Planning Validation Requirements July 2023'. The yoursay page says the consultation ran 16 March-14 April 2023.

issues.detail: Householder is marked '(none) - national requirements only', but the list applies several local requirements to all applications, householder included: L1 Block plan (unless the footprint does not change), L2 Elevations, L3 Floor plans, L4 Roof plans (any roof creation or alteration), L5 Sections (changing levels or sloping site), L9 Tree survey, L15 FRA (Flood Zones 2/3 including minor development) and L18 Heritage Statement.
issues.evidence: L1: 'All applications except where there is no proposed change to the footprint'. L15 covers Flood Zones 2 or 3 'including minor development and change of use'.

issues.detail: 'Floor plans / Elevations' is placed under Outline because the word 'outline' appears in the text, but the source excludes outline applications where appearance is reserved. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' is also placed under Outline only, although N6 applies to any EIA development (Schedule 1/2).
issues.evidence: L2: 'All applications proposing new building or alterations to the exterior of existing buildings (except outline applications where 'appearance' is reserved)'. N6: EIA applications for Schedule 1 or 2 projects under the 2017 Regulations.

issues.detail: All 24 Full planning rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', and the other application types are left as '(none)'. Examples: L9 Tree survey applies to 'All tree work applications', but Works to trees is '(none)'. L18 Heritage Statement and N4 DAS apply to listed building consent, but Listed building consent is '(none)'. L28 Telecommunications supplementary information applies to telecoms development.
issues.evidence: L9 Arboricultural/Tree Survey: 'All tree work applications and any application where there are trees, within or adjacent to a site...'

issues.detail: Local requirements not captured as rows: L3 Floor plans (new or amended floorspace; only captured jointly with elevations under Outline); L4 Roof plans (any creation or alteration of a roof); L5 Sections (changing ground levels or sloping site); L7 Supporting Planning Statement (major development and key policy issues such as loss of employment, affordable housing, loss of retail or open space); L8 Air Quality Assessment (significant air quality impact or pollutants); L11 Car Parking Management Strategy (50 or more parking spaces); L14 Daylight/Sunlight Assessment (potential harm to neighbours' light; major residential); L21 Habitats Regulations Assessment Report (any application that might significantly affect Benfleet and Southend Marshes or another protected site; only garbled fragments in tab_items); L23 Recycling/Waste Management Strategy (all major development); L24 Statement of Community Involvement (major or controversial applications); L28 Telecommunications supplementary information; L31 Ventilation/Extraction details (ventilation, air conditioning, extraction or refrigeration equipment proposed); L33 Agricultural Land Impact Assessment (BMV agricultural land on the proposals map).
issues.evidence: Local Requirements L1-L33 in the July 2023 list, e.g. 'L11 Car Parking Management Strategy' (50+ spaces) and 'L31 Ventilation/Extraction System Details'.

issues.detail: The 'Noise Impact Assessment' trigger is copied from the Lighting Assessment ('Should include details of the proposed lighting scheme...'). The real L20 trigger is a significant impact on residential amenity (e.g. bars or nightclubs) or noise-sensitive uses near noise sources.
issues.evidence: Grokbot: 'Noise Impact Assessment/ Acoustic Report ... Should include details of the proposed lighting scheme'. The source's L20 covers significant impact on residential amenity.

issues.detail: The 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' trigger is waste text taken from L23 ('How refuse and recycling will be stored and collected'). The L26 Sustainability Statement trigger is all new development creating additional residential and/or commercial units.
issues.evidence: L26 Sustainability Statement: all new development creating additional residential and/or commercial units.

issues.detail: The BNG trigger ('the biodiversity net gain condition must be discharged before the development can begin') does not say when BNG is needed. The source says all major applications from 1 Nov 2023 and all developments from 1 Apr 2024 unless exempt. Those dates are pre-legislation and now superseded (statutory BNG started 12 Feb 2024 for majors and 2 Apr 2024 for small sites).
issues.evidence: L10b Biodiversity Net Gain: all major applications from 1 November 2023; all developments from 1 April 2024, unless exempted.

issues.detail: The 'Transport Assessment / Transport Statement' and 'Travel Plan' rows both use the L29 Transport Statement trigger ('relatively small transport implications'). The L30 Transport Assessment (including Travel Plan) trigger, significant transport implications per the Appendix 1 thresholds (e.g. 50+ dwellings, 100+ hotel bedrooms, 2,500+ sqm business), is missing.
issues.evidence: Appendix 1: Residential (C3) Transport Statement 20-49 dwellings, Transport Assessment 50+ dwellings.

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are fragments or 'what is required' text, not when the requirement applies. CIL is a table-of-contents line (should be: a new dwelling of any size or 100 sqm+ new floorspace). DAS is just column headers. Block plan is an article 5(3) fragment. Biodiversity is cut off at 'Where the development will affect'. Viability omits 'over 10 units or 1,000 sqm'. HIA omits '>100 residential units and/or 10,000 sqm commercial'. Retail omits '>2,500 sqm outside the Town Centre Primary Shopping Area'. Foul sewage omits 'All major development'. Fire Statement gives purpose text instead of 18m+/7+ storeys with 2+ dwellings. Visibility splays and Sequential/Exception Test are sentence fragments.
issues.evidence: Grokbot CIL trigger: 'Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Additional Information Requirement Form......... 21 Page 3 L13: Contaminated Land Assessment ....'

issues.detail: The 'Transport Assessment / Transport Statement' and 'Travel Plan' rows have the same trigger text, taken from L29.
issues.evidence: Both rows: 'Transport Statement (including Travel Plan Statement) ... A transport statement will be required for development with relatively small transport implications as set out in Appendix 1.'

issues.detail: Several tab_items are not requirements. 'Where to look for further information Viability - GOV.UK (... rics.org) Policy Driver...' is reference text. 'Any sensitive personal information should not be made public' and 'For major/complex applications we may request additional sets ... USB memory stick' are process text. 'European Site Conservation Objectives ... Page 25 Local Requirements - technical documents:' is a page or heading fragment. 'Special Protection Areas (SPA) requirements of the relevant legislation.' is a fragment. 'Benfleet and Southend Marshes ...' is garbled text interleaved from two columns.
issues.evidence: tab_items, sections 'Submission rules' and 'Policy-driven requirements (all application types)'.

issues.detail: Design and Access Statement (N4), Environmental Statement (N6) and Fire Statement (N7) are national-list items but are presented as local requirements under Full planning.
issues.evidence: The source groups these under 'National Requirements (N1-N7)'.

issues.detail: The council has been Southend-on-Sea City Council since 2022 (the list is issued under that name). The 'Planning page' field is only the site homepage, not the 'Make a planning application' page that links the list.
issues.evidence: Planning page = https://www.southend.gov.uk. The list is linked from https://www.southend.gov.uk/make-planning-application/make-planning-application-2.

summary: Grokbot links the current July 2023 list (still the latest published), but dates it March 2023 from PDF metadata. Its extraction is weak: about 14 local requirements are missing, several triggers are garbled or taken from other items (e.g. Noise uses the lighting text), Householder/LBC/Works to trees are wrongly shown as having no local requirements, and elevations are wrongly placed under Outline.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
